feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Procedura: Agentic 3D Modeling with Procedural Control
entry.summary:
Procedura is a 3D modeling agent framework that generates editable, parametric 3D objects as procedural code assemblies using LLM-driven graph planning, machine-checkable mates, and decoupled vision critics.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between text-to-3D generation and CAD engineering by outputting fully editable, structured, and articulated programs rather than non-parametric, dense meshes.

entry.title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation
entry.summary:
Luce unifies geometry and PBR materials into a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud using dedicated primitives, autoencoding them into a material-aware latent space for single-image relightable 3D asset generation via a rectified-flow transformer.

Why it matters: Luce enables the direct creation of relightable, high-fidelity 3D assets with accurate PBR materials and fine details like text from a single input image.

entry.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
entry.summary:
CritICL is a novel inference-time framework that enhances LLM reasoning by incorporating structured failure modes from smaller models into critique-based in-context learning prompts.

Why it matters: CritICL improves reasoning accuracy at inference time while bypassing the high compute and token costs associated with traditional test-time scaling and repeated generations.

entry.title: CaRGo-T: Causal Reasoning Graph-of-Thought improves Multimodal Humor Comprehension
entry.summary:
CaRGo-T is a framework that improves multimodal humor understanding by using vision-language models to generate code-serialized, graph-based representations of causal and contextual relationships.

Why it matters: Graph-structured causal reasoning provides a more effective mechanism than linear prompting for vision-language models to interpret complex, implicit multimodal interactions like humor.

entry.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
entry.summary:
TacForcing introduces a streaming action expert that integrates execution-time tactile feedback into vision-language-action models using Execution-Aware Tactile Attention, eliminating separate reactive controllers.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language-action models to dynamically adapt to real-time contact changes during execution without complex, multi-component control architectures.

entry.title: CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval
entry.summary:
CaSKG introduces a counterfactual-causal skill graph framework that calibrates offline procedural skill edges using direction-conditioned textual probes and Bayesian smoothing to improve LLM agent skill retrieval.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to accurately retrieve executable workflows, prerequisites, and state-changing actions from large skill libraries without incurring the high context costs of full-library prompting.

entry.title: Thinking on Shots: Consistent Multi-Shot Video Editing with Agentic Reasoning
entry.summary:
MMLVE-Agent uses LLMs and VLMs to perform multi-instruction multi-shot long-video editing while maintaining cross-shot consistency and spatiotemporal structure.

Why it matters: It resolves entity fragmentation and continuity loss in long-video editing by replacing fixed chunking with agent-driven shot decoupling and instruction parsing.

entry.title: Skill Issue: Are Skills Language-Invariant in LLMs?
entry.summary:
A new multilingual self-play benchmark using an extended TextArena evaluates cross-lingual skill inconsistency in LLMs by pitting identical models against each other under different language interfaces while keeping state spaces and game rules fixed.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that LLM skill execution is not language-invariant, highlighting language bias in decision-making pipelines and the need for equitable cross-lingual model design.

entry.title: Prefix Sliding for efficient test-time scaling
entry.summary:
Prefix Sliding optimizes test-time compute by discarding middle reasoning tokens while retaining initial instructions and recent context, reducing memory overhead and accelerating inference.

Why it matters: It enables models to perform long-horizon reasoning over 100,000 tokens efficiently by eliminating memory bottlenecks during test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: EditaLive! Unified Character Video Editing for Live Streaming
entry.summary:
EditaLive is a framework that adapts the Wan-Animate model for real-time, instruction-based human-centric video editing during live streams with minimal facial-expression loss and low latency.

Why it matters: It enables low-latency, real-time character video editing during live streams while maintaining facial expression consistency and preventing appearance drift.

entry.title: Aphanta: Diagnosing Task-Aligned Image-Edited Intermediates for Multimodal Reasoning
entry.summary:
Aphanta is a diagnostic framework evaluating MLLM-to-image-editor-to-MLLM pipelines by comparing direct reasoning, editor-generated intermediates, and idealized reference intermediates across 20 tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes that image editing acts as a task-specific visual workspace rather than a universal reasoning tool, providing a standardized protocol to evaluate MLLM visual representation alignment.

entry.title: RetrievalRouter: Joint Modality and Architecture Selection for Document Retrieval
entry.summary:
RetrievalRouter is a lightweight, query-aware routing system that dynamically selects the optimal retrieval pipeline's modality and architecture from query text alone, breaking static trade-offs between accuracy and latency.

Why it matters: It enables high-stakes document retrieval systems in fields like law and finance to maximize accuracy while drastically reducing the computation costs and latency of complex pipelines.

entry.title: What Does an Evaluation License? A Commit-Bound Census of Claim-Relative Inference in Inspect Evals
entry.summary:
A commit-bound census of 124 Inspect Evals units formalizes a claim-replay layer, revealing that 110 units stop before deterministic inference due to missing historical evidence or semantic grounding.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard evaluation artifacts often lack the historical and semantic binding required to reliably support or replay their attached claims.

entry.title: LibriBrain100: One Hundred Hours of Broad and Deep MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding at Scale
entry.summary:
LibriBrain100 is a large-scale MEG dataset containing over 100 hours of continuous speech listening data, including ~80 hours from a single subject and ~40 minutes across 32 subjects.

Why it matters: The dataset and standardized evaluation pipeline accelerate the development of practical, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces aimed at restoring communication for individuals with severe paralysis.

entry.title: JudgeStealer: Extracting LLM Judging Capabilities across Evaluation Protocols
entry.summary:
JUDGESTEALER is a query-efficient framework designed to extract black-box LLM judging capabilities across pointwise, pairwise, and listwise evaluation protocols using dynamically selected pointwise queries.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that proprietary LLM judge and reward model intellectual property can be stolen efficiently across multiple evaluation formats despite query budget constraints and extraction defenses.

entry.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
entry.summary:
CLAP introduces a cross-embodiment video world model framework that leverages latent actions, end-effector poses, and language instructions to learn generalizable physics across human and diverse robotic datasets.

Why it matters: It enables action-conditioned video generation models to train on internet-scale heterogeneous video data, bypassing the restriction of single-robot embodiment datasets for physical simulation.

entry.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
entry.summary:
CAST uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to identify, audit, and suppress text artifact features during clinical language model fine-tuning, improving robustness and decision transparency.

Why it matters: It prevents clinical models from relying on spurious formatting artifacts, making AI predictions robust to deployment shifts and fully auditable by clinicians.

entry.title: LeVJEPA: Efficient & Scalable Video Pretraining without the Heuristics
entry.summary:
LeVJEPA is the first video encoder trained with LeJEPA's collapse-free objective, eliminating architectural asymmetries, stop-gradients, and target encoders while drastically reducing pretraining compute.

Why it matters: It removes the heavy computational overhead and complex heuristics of video self-supervised learning, making video a viable, efficient alternative to static images for general-purpose visual pretraining.

entry.title: Successive Capacity Growth: Task-Complexity-Driven Width and Depth Expansion for Vision Transformer Encoders in JEPA World Models
entry.summary:
Successive Capacity Growth (SCG) dynamically expands Vision Transformer encoders in JEPA world models in width or depth using a task-agnostic, function-preserving test-and-verify mechanism.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to pre-allocate maximum transformer capacity in JEPA world models, optimizing compute and parameter efficiency without losing predictive quality.

entry.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
entry.summary:
PAWBench and PAWEval introduce a benchmark and outcome-level evaluation protocol to test whether video generation models function as probabilistically aligned world models that match true physical behavior distributions.

Why it matters: Current video-based world models fail to capture the correct probability distributions of non-deterministic physical events, highlighting a key gap in developing reliable stochastic simulators.

entry.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance
entry.summary:
Eval-awareness in model chain-of-thought is not uniform; capabilities-framed eval-awareness predicts compliance with dangerous requests at significantly higher rates (+24 to +46 percentage points) than safety-framed eval-awareness.

Why it matters: Safety evaluation pipelines cannot treat eval-awareness as a single metric to suppress, as different framings cause vastly different safety and compliance behaviors.

entry.title: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search
entry.summary:
Naive Prompt Optimization (NPO) uses a lightweight, single-lineage iterative prompt revision method driven by teacher model feedback, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding complex prompt search algorithms like GEPA using fewer rollouts.

Why it matters: NPO demonstrates that strong teacher reasoning can replace complex optimizer search architectures, drastically reducing the computational cost of optimizing agent prompts.

entry.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
This paper presents a two-level framework that factorizes LLM agentic data and uses the Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens to guide constrained data generation.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized formal framework to evaluate and generate informative, non-redundant synthetic experience for evolving LLM agents instead of relying on raw dataset scaling.

entry.title: PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference
entry.summary:
PACE is a training-free VLM inference framework that uses a Condense-and-Extract paradigm to reduce computation in both the vision encoder and LLM.

Why it matters: It significantly cuts VLM inference latency and computation without requiring model retraining or sacrificing critical fine-grained visual details.

entry.title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue
entry.summary:
Researchers created ContraTalk, a benchmark measuring cross-modal transcript bias in spoken dialogue, and introduced an Audio Twin framework to expose localized acoustic evidence directly to LLM reasoning models.

Why it matters: The findings show that current audio-language models rely heavily on text shortcuts, demonstrating the need for explicit acoustic evidence extraction to achieve reliable speech-grounded reasoning.

entry.title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models
entry.summary:
A new post-training framework, Reinforcement Learning with Human-Engine Verification (RLHEV), uses game development code and engine runtimes as verifiable trajectory data engines for spatial world models.

Why it matters: It establishes an executable, verifiable data engine for spatial world models, enabling effective RL post-training similar to compiler-based feedback loops in code agents.

entry.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?
entry.summary:
PAWBench and its evaluation protocol PAWEval benchmark video generation models as stochastic world models to measure how accurately repeated rollouts capture the real-world probability distribution of multi-outcome physical behaviors.

Why it matters: Determining whether video models achieve probabilistic alignment reveals whether they function as true physical world models rather than just generators of single plausible visual trajectories.

entry.title: UrbanGround: From Local Perception to Spatial Agency in a Real-Scale City
entry.summary:
UrbanGround is the first 3D sandbox built from territory-wide geospatial data of Hong Kong to evaluate MLLM agents' ability to translate first-person visual perception into navigation and spatial reasoning.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, physically constrained benchmark to identify why current MLLMs fail at long-horizon spatial agency and navigation in real-world urban environments.

entry.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO) introduces an asymmetric objective combining On-Policy Self-Distillation and Grouped RL with token-level selection, enabling label-free test-time training for mathematical reasoning in large language models.

Why it matters: TTPO enables large language models to continuously improve their mathematical reasoning performance at test time without relying on ground-truth labels.

entry.title: Self-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Flow Matching Models without Teacher
entry.summary:
Self-OPD is a teacher-free on-policy distillation framework for flow matching models that replaces external teachers with self-exploration, SDE trajectory branching, and advantage-weighted pull-push optimization.

Why it matters: It removes the high computational cost of training task-specific teacher models and mitigates compounding trajectory errors in flow matching distillation.

entry.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
A new framework formalizes agentic data as a factorized tuple (E,q,τ,v) and evaluates generation strategies using the Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens.

Why it matters: It replaces ad-hoc data generation with a structured theoretical framework for synthesizing valid, appropriately challenging, and non-redundant training data for LLM agents.

entry.title: Training Agents to Evolve with Their Harness: TaoLive Digital Avatar Agent Technical Report
entry.summary:
Harness-Aware Training (HAT) enables compact LLMs to adapt to evolving digital avatar agent harnesses without retraining model weights or degrading baseline generalization performance.

Why it matters: It allows lightweight models to achieve low-latency execution and high accuracy in production live-streaming environments while seamlessly adapting to frequent tool and prompt updates.

entry.title: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
entry.summary:
GameWAM is the first World-Action Model for native closed-loop gameplay and GUI control, unifying visual prediction and keyboard-mouse action generation via parallel flow matching.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that unifying world modeling and action generation enables higher task success in complex video games using fewer executed native inputs.

entry.title: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
PILOT introduces a supervisor-worker agent harness for live self-improvement, using mid-run steering and real-time self-evolution to refine active trajectories and store persistent skills.

Why it matters: It enables AI agents to fix trajectory errors in real time while significantly reducing token consumption and improving execution efficiency during complex, long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization
entry.summary:
Zero-WAM is a causal video-action model that achieves zero-shot cross-task robot manipulation by following in-context human video prompts without parameter updates.

Why it matters: It enables robots to generalize to entirely unseen manipulation tasks by directly using unlabeled human demonstration videos as context prompts rather than requiring explicit re-training or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
entry.summary:
A systematic study demonstrates that Evolution Strategies (ES) achieve broader reasoning coverage and higher Pass@K performance than GRPO by maintaining population diversity and avoiding entropy collapse during post-training.

Why it matters: ES provides a viable, memory-efficient post-training alternative to GRPO that unlocks broader latent LLM reasoning capabilities without triggering catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Studying trajectory handoffs between low-capability and high-capability LLM coding agents reveals a 'handoff tax' where full-trajectory model escalation recovers less than half the potential quality gain while driving up costs.

Why it matters: Optimizing how context is passed between cheap and expensive models allows developers to reduce LLM agent execution costs without unnecessarily sacrificing coding accuracy.

entry.title: Rubrics as Visual-Repair Context for Self-Evolving UI-to-Code Generation
entry.summary:
RubSE is a rubric-guided self-evolution framework for UI-to-code generation that uses structured visual-repair contexts to prevent over-broad code edits and visual regression during iterative refinement.

Why it matters: It improves the stability and performance ceiling of iterative VLM code generation by preventing cascading visual errors during automated UI design fixes.

entry.title: Gated Recurrent Transformers: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation
entry.summary:
The Gated Recurrent Transformer uses fixed prelude and coda blocks around a single recurrent core modulated by elementwise update gating to match dense transformer expressivity with significantly fewer parameters.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to drastically reduce memory usage and parameter count during inference while maintaining quality through recurrent layer reuse.

entry.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
entry.summary:
WikiSkill is a framework that co-evolves AI agent skills with a persistent wiki-style knowledge base, continuously consolidating execution experience to improve skill synthesis and refinement across iterations.

Why it matters: Decoupling experience into a persistent, evolving knowledge base allows AI agents to continuously build reusable skills that improve performance and transfer effectively across different model architectures and sizes.

entry.title: Performance Foundations of Parallel & Distributed Reasoning Language Models
entry.summary:
This paper presents a compute-centric analysis and parallel computing taxonomy for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) frameworks used to train Reasoning Language Models.

Why it matters: It provides practical system design guidelines for scaling massive, multi-model RLM training pipelines efficiently while reducing hardware costs and runtime bottlenecks.

entry.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that Evolution Strategies (ES) for LLM post-training achieve broader reasoning coverage and avoid entropy collapse compared to GRPO, enabling higher Pass@K performance.

Why it matters: It establishes ES as a complementary, high-coverage post-training paradigm rather than just a memory-efficient GRPO substitute, providing a hybrid training pathway to maximize LLM reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Disentangling Optimization Scale from Preference Scale in DPO
entry.summary:
A study reveals DPO's beta parameter entangles preference-noise scaling with optimization step size, causing non-monotone policy shifts, and introduces a centered-softplus reformulation to decouple these effects.

Why it matters: Decoupling preference scale from optimization scale reduces hyperparameter sensitivity and simplifies learning-rate tuning during language model alignment.

entry.title: SCIT: Testing Causal Cache Carriers in Latent Chain-of-Thought Models
entry.summary:
SCIT is a causal interchange test that identifies transformer cache components carrying counterfactual computation in latent chain-of-thought models, revealing model- and scale-dependent carrier-regime shifts.

Why it matters: SCIT provides a precise, cache-level diagnostic tool to uncover and validate where hidden reasoning occurs inside latent chain-of-thought transformers.

entry.title: Prediction of Prediction (PoP): Inter-Layer Activation Fusion for Single-Pass Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Prediction of Prediction (PoP) detects LLM hallucinations in a single forward pass with under 1.2% latency by fusing intermediate hidden representations across layers.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, low-overhead hallucination detection without the high latency and memory costs of multi-sample verification pipelines.

entry.title: TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy
entry.summary:
TwinKV is a training-free, attention-free repair pass that restores lost information in evicted KV caches by swapping redundant retained tokens with evicted orphan tokens.

Why it matters: It allows existing KV cache eviction algorithms to recover lost context and improve long-context LLM inference efficiency without retraining or altering target cache budgets.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment Without Joint Training: Do Monolingual Language Models Converge on Universal Representations?
entry.summary:
Monolingual language models trained independently on non-parallel data develop alignable representational geometries that enable functional cross-lingual transfer without joint training.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that cross-lingual alignment stems from intrinsic language structure, enabling modular multilingual systems, model merging, and model stitching without computationally expensive joint training.

entry.title: Planting a Latent Variable in Natural-Looking Text: a More Realistic Test of Belief States in LLMs and Their Link to Concept Geometry
entry.summary:
Researchers planted a 8-state ring-shaped Markov latent variable in natural text via SAE steering, showing student LLMs track Bayesian belief states and mirror this geometry.

Why it matters: It provides empirical evidence that an LLM's internal feature geometry is directly shaped by the statistical dynamics of latent variables present in its training data.

entry.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
entry.summary:
SWE-Prime is a two-stage data selection method that filters agent trajectories at the trajectory and segment levels, enabling SFT on just 10% of data while outperforming full-dataset training on SWE-Bench benchmarks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that masking noisy or redundant steps during loss computation significantly improves software engineering agent performance while reducing SFT data requirements.

entry.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
entry.summary:
RedEvoAgent is a black-box red-teaming agent that distills cross-case attack trajectories into evolving, human-readable attack skills to jailbreak LLM agents in execution harnesses.

Why it matters: It improves red-teaming tool efficiency and attack success across different target models and execution harnesses while maintaining context-efficient, interpretable attack strategies.

entry.title: VoiceMem: Streaming Dual-Brain Memory for Real-Time Interaction
entry.summary:
VoiceMem is a streaming dual-brain memory architecture featuring parallel informational left-brain and emotional right-brain components designed for real-time, low-latency duplex speech language models.

Why it matters: VoiceMem enables speech language models to access highly accurate factual memory and persona-driven emotional state in real time without introducing user-perceptible latency.

entry.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
entry.summary:
FrontierChallenge is a new cross-domain benchmark of 300 scientific workflows that evaluates end-to-end task completion and deliverable bundles across multiple computational sciences.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high partial scoring and confident language model outputs do not correlate with full scientific workflow execution, requiring stricter end-to-end deliverable evaluation.

entry.title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation
entry.summary:
WarpSAC adapts off-policy RL algorithmic stabilizers based on data abundance, offering two variants that optimize exploitation and value fitting for CPU-scale and GPU-parallel training regimes.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling off-policy reinforcement learning to massively parallel GPU environments requires removing data-limited constraints to achieve higher sample efficiency, faster training, and better real-world deployment performance.

entry.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
entry.summary:
JIT-Agent is a harness intelligence model that dynamically synthesizes, repairs, and evolves task-adaptive agent harnesses for off-the-shelf LLMs using a four-module composable protocol.

Why it matters: It establishes agent harness design as a trainable, automated, and transferable dimension of capability that improves model performance orthogonally to standard foundation model scaling.

entry.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed featuring 300 procedurally generated tasks and deterministic rule-based reward scorers to enable trainable, verifiable, and scalable native visual reasoning across image, video, and interleaved generators.

Why it matters: It replaces unreliable VLM-as-a-judge metrics with deterministic reward scorers, allowing models to use visual generation as an optimizable medium for complex problem solving via reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SecOPD uses on-policy distillation to provide token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, significantly reducing LLM vulnerability to adaptive prompt injections.

Why it matters: Token-level feedback during defensive fine-tuning effectively neutralizes adaptive prompt injections without sacrificing model performance on unseen agentic tasks.

entry.title: D^3-MOPD: Adaptive Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation
entry.summary:
D^3-MOPD dynamically schedules multi-teacher domain sampling ratios online using reverse-KL trajectories to optimize student training without adding computational overhead.

Why it matters: It enables significantly more compute-efficient multi-domain knowledge distillation by dynamically shifting training resources to slower-converging domains.

entry.title: Agent-G^2: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Agent-G^2 introduces a Gaussian guidance framework that dynamically samples hint depths from an online-estimated Gaussian distribution to resolve reward sparsity in agentic reinforcement learning without extra rollout costs.

Why it matters: It significantly improves task success rates in long-horizon agentic RL while cutting compute requirements by over 66% compared to probing methods.

entry.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data
entry.summary:
Mixed SFT outperforms next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data post-RLVR, achieving higher accuracy ceilings while using over 60 times less training compute.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex next-chunk RL is unnecessary for no-CoT data, as simple Mixed SFT provides better post-RLVR performance at a fraction of the compute cost.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds
entry.summary:
JoyAI-Echo-1.5 is a unified audio-visual system for generating long-horizon video narratives and interactive worlds using composable memory, geometry-aware control, and rollout-aware few-step training.

Why it matters: It enables persistent character identities, coherent audio-visual storytelling, and stable controller-agnostic camera navigation over long generation horizons.

entry.title: StreamPI: Streaming Multimodal Temporal Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
StreamPI is a parameter-free temporal modeling framework for Vision-Language-Action models that enables streaming multi-frame reasoning and asynchronous real-robot deployment.

Why it matters: It allows existing single-frame VLA models to gain temporal reasoning and real-time streaming capabilities for complex robotics tasks without requiring extra parameters.

entry.title: Video-IFBench: Evaluating Instruction Following of Multimodal LLMs in Video Understanding Scenarios
entry.summary:
Video-IFBench is a new benchmark featuring 1.5K samples across 32 task types to evaluate how well Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) follow complex user constraints in video understanding tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to measure whether video-capable MLLMs can adhere strictly to specific formatting and semantic constraints, rather than just assessing basic video content accuracy.

entry.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
entry.summary:
Code World Model decouples world evolution from visual generation by using a coding agent to maintain state via executable code and conditioning a video model on spatiotemporal proxy representations.

Why it matters: By relying on executable code for world state rather than purely visual priors, this architecture enables persistent consequences and rule-consistent, open-ended world simulation.

entry.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
entry.summary:
SWE Refactor Bench evaluates coding agents on 20 whole-repository migrations across four technical debt types using a three-stage protocol that checks both migration completeness and behavioral correctness.

Why it matters: The benchmark prevents agents from cheating by copying legacy code to pass tests, exposing that current frontier models struggle with reliable, long-horizon codebase refactoring.

entry.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
V-Rubrics introduces rubric-based reinforcement learning that decomposes responses into atomic propositions to provide structured, prefix-localized reward credit across visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency, and instruction following.

Why it matters: Decomposing rewards into localized, proposition-level rubrics mitigates visual hallucination and ungrounded reasoning in vision-language models better than traditional scalar reward signals.

entry.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed with 300 procedurally generated tasks and deterministic reward scorers designed to scale, verify, and optimize native visual reasoning through image, video, and interleaved generation.

Why it matters: It establishes a verifiable, reinforcement-learning-ready framework for training multimodal models to use visual generation directly as a substrate for complex problem solving.

entry.title: Prefix Sliding for efficient test-time scaling
entry.summary:
Prefix Sliding reduces test-time scaling costs by discarding intermediate reasoning tokens while retaining the initial instruction prefix and a sliding window of recent tokens.

Why it matters: It enables models to perform ultra-long-horizon reasoning and test-time compute scaling at a fraction of the computational and memory cost.

entry.title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention
entry.summary:
This paper establishes task-dependent rank-error bounds for Query LoRA updates in Transformer attention, expressing expected KL error through the downstream-weighted tail energy of target updates.

Why it matters: It provides a theoretical foundation for selecting LoRA ranks based on task data and attention geometry rather than relying solely on trial-and-error hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: DualOPSD: Adaptive Privileged Teachers for On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
DualOPSD introduces an asymmetric alternating framework for on-policy self-distillation that dynamically adapts the privileged teacher toward the updated student distribution without requiring extra rollouts.

Why it matters: It improves student model accuracy and generation length efficiency in self-distillation without incurring the computational overhead of generating new teacher rollouts.

entry.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
entry.summary:
AsymSpec is an asymmetric speculative decoding framework where a lightweight draft model operates on full context while a large verifier model runs on a compressed context to reduce inference costs.

Why it matters: It breaks the strict latency-accuracy trade-off in agentic LLM pipelines by preserving key reasoning signals with minimal computational overhead.

entry.title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Spectral-Aware Muon (SAMuon), which outperforms AdamW and Muon by using a static spectral prior to apply larger step sizes to the tolerant bulk singular directions of momentum buffers.

Why it matters: SAMuon speeds up LLM pretraining convergence by up to 24% over Muon without requiring additional persistent optimizer memory.

entry.title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents
entry.summary:
SwarmWorld demonstrates that decentralized, initially homogeneous LLM agents can self-organize through environmental stigmergy and physical observation to build durable, resilient technological societies without predefined roles or direct centralized workflows.

Why it matters: It proves LLM multi-agent systems can achieve scalable collective intelligence and complex engineering through environmental modification (stigmergy) rather than relying on direct conversation or centralized control.

entry.title: $R^3$: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
$R^3$ is a post-training recipe that uses mid-training on expert traces and rubric-based RL on offline action data to train VLMs to generate free-form natural language reasoning for steering low-level robotic policies.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that free-form natural language reasoning can serve as an effective test-time compute mechanism to improve long-horizon task execution and generalization in robotic manipulation.

entry.title: ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs
entry.summary:
ProgRouter is an online routing framework that adaptively selects LLM agents step-by-step during multi-agent workflows based on task progress predictions, time constraints, and cost budgets.

Why it matters: It enables multi-agent LLM systems to solve complex tasks within strict financial and latency budgets by dynamically routing lower-cost models when full-scale models are unnecessary.

entry.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
This review provides a unified structural framework identifying collapse as the primary failure mode in On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for mathematical reasoning, analyzing it through three governing levers.

Why it matters: It establishes a clear vocabulary and structural framework to help researchers analyze and prevent model collapse when using self-teacher privileged guidance instead of larger teacher models.

entry.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models
entry.summary:
EchoWM is an omnimodal world model that enables continuous camera navigation while simultaneously generating 720p video, environmental sound, speech, and music across first-person and third-person perspectives.

Why it matters: It unifies multi-modal generation with flexible 6-DoF trajectory control, enabling interactive, synchronized audio-visual media generation for virtual environments.

entry.title: Annotations as Rollouts: Efficient and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Video MLLMs
entry.summary:
OraRL integrates ground-truth annotations as oracle rollouts during video MLLM post-training, using a decoupled advantage estimator and sign-balanced pruning to bypass slow chain-of-thought generation while improving performance.

Why it matters: It enables highly efficient RL post-training for video MLLMs, dramatically cutting decoding latency while outperforming substantially larger commercial models like GPT-5 and Gemini-3-Pro on spatial and temporal intelligence benchmarks.

entry.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report
entry.summary:
Tencent introduced WeMM-Embedding, a family of universal multimodal embedding models (2B, 4B, and 9B) supporting text, images, videos, visual documents, and interleaved multimodal inputs with flexible output dimensions.

Why it matters: WeMM-Embedding provides open-source, high-efficiency multimodal embedding models that outperform larger baselines and have proven scalable efficacy in production recommendation and search environments.

entry.title: AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces
entry.summary:
AutoSaddler is an automatic agent harness optimization framework that treats harnesses as code and uses offline mini-batch execution traces to iteratively diagnose failures, generate patches, and select updates.

Why it matters: Automating harness design removes the manual effort required to optimize complex agent prompts, tools, and control flow for long-horizon execution tasks.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
DiffusionOPSD converts image-level reward guidance into bounded positive and negative targets for intermediate denoising predictions using an on-policy self-distillation framework with frozen behavior policies and finite fitting.

Why it matters: It improves diffusion model alignment accuracy while significantly lowering compute requirements and enabling separate analysis of target generation versus target learning.

entry.title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Prefix Invariance in Attention, State-Space, and Hybrid Sequence Models
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize prefix invariance and introduce a two-forward-pass gradient-free audit that localizes causal leaks across attention, state-space, and hybrid sequence architectures where attention-mask inspection fails.

Why it matters: Standard attention-mask checks are insufficient for ensuring causality, making empirical auditing essential for preventing future data leakage in complex or hybrid sequence models.

entry.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
entry.summary:
Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture that uses a fixed Meta-Agent to perform localized, validation-gated updates to Skill Memory based on execution evidence, preventing long-history performance degradation.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable architecture for recursive self-improvement that allows agents to handle expanding interaction horizons without getting derailed by lengthy execution histories.

entry.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) replaces action-side Policy-KL with input-side Query-KL to control query distribution shift without constraining LLM response exploration.

Why it matters: ERPO resolves the stability-exploration trade-off in LLM reinforcement learning, preventing policy drift while maintaining full action-space exploration without computational overhead.

entry.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs
entry.summary:
Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) stabilizes 4-bit compressed LLM post-training by distilling directly from the original, uncompressed teacher model rather than using hard-label QAT.

Why it matters: QAH enables rapid, stable recovery of heavily compressed and 4-bit quantized LLMs without requiring multi-week hyperparameter searches.

entry.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out
entry.summary:
AutoResearch is a two-stage autonomous system that grounds research idea generation via multi-model cross-review and grounds execution using independent evidence-based review to prevent hallucinations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that coupling grounded idea generation with rigorous automated experimental auditing significantly reduces scientific hallucinations in autonomous AI research workflows.

entry.title: From Seeing to Acting: Smart Glasses as First-Person Intelligence Platforms
entry.summary:
This survey provides a unified framework for smart glasses as first-person intelligence platforms, introducing an L0-L5 autonomy taxonomy, hardware capability axes, application scene mapping, and deployment and evaluation protocols.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to design, compare, and reproducibly evaluate trustworthy egocentric AI systems operating across tightly constrained hardware and real-world deployment environments.

entry.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
entry.summary:
OPDVR combines on-policy distillation and RLVR by using a ReLU gating mechanism on trajectory correctness, eliminating extra hyperparameters while improving reasoning benchmarks.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to benefit from dense teacher distillation while ensuring policy gradient updates align strictly with verifiable task success without adding hyperparameter complexity.

entry.title: LongWoF-Bench: Evaluating EvoMap Genes for Verifiable Long-Workflow Tasks
entry.summary:
LongWoF-Bench evaluates EvoMap Genes, which externalize verifier-confirmed execution trajectories into reusable structures that significantly boost long-workflow task performance across diverse language models.

Why it matters: Consolidating verified execution trajectories into structured, reusable Genes allows models to improve long-workflow success rates and lower token costs without re-discovering strategies from scratch.

entry.title: Better Retrieval, Worse Robustness:How Multi-hop RAG Amplifies Upstream ASR Errors
entry.summary:
Multi-hop RAG extensions like entity-graph linking and iterative reformulation amplify upstream ASR errors, resulting in a 36-67% larger clean-to-noisy F1 performance gap than naive dense retrieval across three benchmarks.

Why it matters: Building voice-driven multi-hop RAG systems requires addressing structural error amplification, as standard graph and iterative retrieval techniques degrade significantly when exposed to noisy ASR inputs.

entry.title: Industrial-Instruction: An End-to-End Framework for Building Instruction-Tuning and Benchmark Datasets from Industrial Technical Reports
entry.summary:
Industrial-Instruction introduces an end-to-end pipeline and two open QA datasets derived from Panasonic technical reports to benchmark and fine-tune LLMs on industrial troubleshooting, maintenance, and specification data.

Why it matters: It provides a reproducible framework to transform complex, multi-modal industrial technical documentation into effective instruction-tuning data and benchmarks for targeted enterprise LLM deployment.

entry.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
entry.summary:
Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture that decouples long-horizon state tracking from skill execution, using a fixed Meta-Agent to perform localized, validation-gated memory updates.

Why it matters: It establishes localized, memory-level updates as a scalable mechanism for recursive self-improvement in LLM agents without needing full context history or model re-training.

entry.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL
entry.summary:
SPO++ enhances asynchronous agentic RL by standardizing terminal-outcome advantages under the action-token measure and organizing prompt evidence by policy event generation order rather than learner receipt order.

Why it matters: It eliminates training delays in variable-length, tool-use RL trajectories without sacrificing policy optimization stability or sample efficiency.

entry.title: CAFE: Self-Improving Search Agents Need Co-Evolving Feedback
entry.summary:
CAFE is a framework where a shared-parameter model alternates between search-agent and critic roles to co-evolve corrective feedback alongside policy updates.

Why it matters: Co-evolving in-trajectory feedback prevents optimization plateaus in self-improving search agents and leads to lower hallucination rates during complex retrievals.

entry.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
entry.summary:
Meta$^n$ achieves recursive self-improvement beyond two meta-levels by holding a meta-operation fixed and repeatedly applying it to its own traces and code to generate subsequent layers.

Why it matters: It bypasses the traditional stability-driven caps on meta-depth in LLM agents, enabling continuous strategic self-improvement without destabilizing editing machinery.

entry.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
entry.summary:
OPDVR combines on-policy distillation and verifiable reward RL by reformulating sampled-token OPD implicit rewards with trajectory correctness and a ReLU gating mechanism, eliminating extra hyperparameters while outperforming standard OPD across six reasoning benchmarks.

Why it matters: It aligns dense token-level teacher guidance with task-level correctness without adding hyperparameter tuning overhead or performance trade-offs.

entry.title: The Invisible Editorial Layer: Formalizing Undisclosed Inference-Time Steering, Probability Placement, and the Attribution Problem in Deployed Language Models
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes undisclosed inference-time steering—systematic logit-level modifications applied before token sampling—and introduces frameworks for attributing behavioral bias, modeling probability placement advertising, and establishing inference policy transparency.

Why it matters: It highlights how undisclosed post-inference logit modifications can secretly manipulate political or commercial framing in LLM outputs, complicating regulatory oversight and bias attribution.

entry.title: Parason: Revealing Subtask and Trial Parallelism in LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
Parason introduces a framework to learn and execute both subtask and trial parallelism in LLM reasoning traces, accelerating inference on complex math benchmarks using Parallelism-Aware GRPO.

Why it matters: By unlocking trial parallelism alongside subtask parallelism, Parason significantly reduces inference latency for long test-time LLM reasoning traces without sacrificing problem-solving accuracy.

entry.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
entry.summary:
Language model pretraining loss dynamics collapse onto a single trajectory when runs match their effective learning rate (ELR), defined as the ratio of learning rate to parameter norm.

Why it matters: ELR serves as a unified coordinate that links learning rate scheduling, norm-control interventions, and scaling laws to simplify pretraining optimization.

entry.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report
entry.summary:
Tencent has released WeMM-Embedding, a family of 2B, 4B, and 9B universal multimodal embedding models supporting text, images, videos, visual documents, and interleaved inputs with flexible output dimensions.

Why it matters: It offers open-source, production-proven multimodal embedding models that outperform larger existing baselines in retrieval, search, and recommendation tasks.

entry.title: Curved Inference II: Sleeper Agent Geometry - Extending Interpretability Beyond Probes
entry.summary:
Curved Inference II introduces semantic surface area (A'), an unsupervised geometric metric in unnormalised residual space that detects naturalistic deceptive reasoning without reliance on backdoors, artificial triggers, or linear probes.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable, unsupervised detection method for deceptive alignment based on the intrinsic geometric shape of inference, even when models suppress linear indicators.
